      "# AGENTS.md\n\n## Build / Lint / Test / Run\n\nNo build step (flat Python/Flask project, no compiler/bundler).\n\n```bash\n# Run the full pytest suite (21 cases: path-guard traversal protection,\n# MFDB manifest/entity validation) \u2014 operates on a temp copy, never touches\n# the live storage/mfdb/ tree directly:\ncd tests && python3 -m pytest -v\n\n# Syntax check any file before shipping it:\npython3 -m py_compile src/web/BEJSON_CMS_Admin.py\n\n# Full smoke-test (syntax is not enough \u2014 a NameError from a missing import\n# only surfaces on actual import, not py_compile):\npython3 -c \"import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src/web'); import BEJSON_CMS_Admin\"\n\n# Run a service directly:\npython3 src/web/BEJSON_CMS_Admin.py\n```\n\nNo linter/formatter config is present in this project \u2014 match the existing\nstyle in the file you're editing rather than introducing a new one.\n\n## Code Style & Conventions\n\n- **Library naming standard**: `lib_bejson_<Family>_<name>.py` for every file\n  under `src/lib/` (e.g. `lib_bejson_Core_bejson_core.py`,\n  `lib_bejson_CMS_cms_core.py`). Existing files predating this standard are\n  NOT renamed in place \u2014 see Library Immutability below.\n- **Snake_case** for all Python variables/functions/fields. **PascalCase**\n  only for BEJSON 104a custom top-level headers.\n- **Self-describing variable names** are required in all new code \u2014 no\n  single-letter locals. This was retrofitted across the whole `src/web/`\n  tree; do not reintroduce short names in new code.\n- **File headers**: every script/module carries a header block \u2014 `Library`,\n  `Family`, `Description`, `Version`, `Date`, `RELATIONAL_ID` (a UUID4 that\n  changes on every real edit, acting as a recency fingerprint). Bump the\n  header version and mint a fresh `RELATIONAL_ID` on every functional change,\n  not on doc-only or logging-only changes.\n- **Library Immutability**: files under `src/lib/` are treated as vendored\n  and are not edited casually. A fix is only applied there after the bug is\n  independently verified (reproduced, not just read), and it gets documented\n  in `docs/` with a dedicated note, per the project's own established\n  practice (see historical entries preserved in `.bejson_project.json`).\n\n## Architectural Rules\n\n- **BEJSON positional integrity**: every entity's `Fields` order must match\n  `Values` order exactly. New fields are appended to the END of the array \u2014\n  never inserted mid-array \u2014 or every existing row's positional indexing\n  breaks.\n- **CMSCore is the only DB interface** application code should use\n  (`get_records` / `add_record` / `update_record` / `delete_record` /\n  `get_field_map` / `sync_manifest_count`). Never read `storage/mfdb/**`\n  files directly \u2014 positional field order is an implementation detail\n  `CMSCore` already resolves by field name.\n- **`update_record()` does a partial merge** \u2014 only keys present in the\n  `updates` dict are touched. Never pass a field \"just to be safe\" unless you\n  intend to overwrite it; a past bug (external-link pages silently converted\n  back to normal pages) came from exactly this mistake.\n- **Two-part page write**: a page is a `PageRecord` row in the manifest PLUS\n  a standalone 104db content file at `storage/mfdb/pages_db/<uuid>.json`.\n  Both are required \u2014 writing one without the other produces a 404 or an\n  empty page.\n- **`sync_count=False` + a single `sync_manifest_count()` call** for any loop\n  that writes multiple records in one request \u2014 per-record fsync was the\n  root cause of a real freeze bug on constrained Android hardware.\n- **Media Library is deliberately low-peak-memory**: single serial background\n  worker (no multiprocessing \u2014 forking duplicates the whole process's memory\n  footprint under pressure), PIL `draft()` mode for large JPEGs, header-only\n  pixel-count caps before any decode, streamed uploads, chunked hashing,\n  server-side pagination. Do not \"optimize\" this back toward parallelism.\n- **Public author bio vs. internal AI persona are separate entities** \u2014\n  `AuthorProfile.auth_bio` (shown on the live site) must never be\n  auto-populated from `AI_Profile`'s internal voice/persona description.\n\n## Directory Map\n\n| Path | Contents |\n|---|---|\n| `src/web/BEJSON_CMS_Admin.py` | Thin entry point \u2014 registers the 4       "README.md",
      ".md",
      "# BEJSON CMS\n\nA personal, self-hosted CMS built on BEJSON/MFDB storage instead of SQL. Every\npage, category, author, ad, nav link, and media record lives as rows inside a\nsingle MFDB manifest (`storage/mfdb/site_master/104a.mfdb.bejson`) backed by\none BEJSON 104 entity file per table. Five Flask apps edit that data; a sixth\npublisher renders it out to a static, dependency-free HTML site.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Blueprint admin app** (`BEJSON_CMS_Admin.py`) \u2014 pages, categories, media\n  library, standalone apps, authors, nav/social/ad config, HTML import, and a\n  publish trigger, split into four Blueprints (System / Content / Media /\n  Interface) registered from one thin entry point.\n- **Canonical Prefix Taxonomy & Strategy Renderers** \u2014 all 10 live entity tables\n  use canonical prefix tags (`page_`, `author_`, `asset_`, `extmedia_`, `ad_`, `cat_`, `nav_`, `sys_`, `social_`, `app_`) and synthetic UUID primary keys (`<prefix>_uuid`). Static rendering features a polymorphic strategy pattern (`BEJSON_CMS_Renderers.py`) for Standard, Video, and Document page types.\n- **Two page editors** \u2014 `BEJSON_CMS_PageEditor.py` (\"V1\") and\n  `BEJSON_CMS_PageEditorV2.py` (\"V2\", API-driven, in active development) \u2014 both\n  read/write the same page content contract and are cross-compatible.\n- **AI Persona Hub** (`BEJSON_CMS_ProfileManager.py`) \u2014 maintains `AI_Profile`\n  records that shape system instructions used by the page editors' AI\n  generation features, kept separate from the public-facing `AuthorProfile`\n  bio shown on the live site.\n- **Static publisher** (`BEJSON_CMS_Publisher.py`) \u2014 renders the full MFDB\n  content set into `storage/builds/` as a static site (dark/light themes,\n  category/page/app feeds, ad zones, generated excerpts, polymorphic page type rendering).\n- **Single-service launcher** (`cms_launcher.sh`) \u2014 kills any other running\n  CMS service before starting the requested one, keeping RAM usage low on\n  constrained devices (Termux/Pydroid3 on Android).\n- **MediaAsset-backed Media Library** \u2014 paginated gallery, hash-dedup upload\n  queue (single serial worker, low peak memory), bulk delete, replace,\n  external-media links, tap-to-zoom lightbox.\n\n## Installation\n\n```bash\n# Python 3.10+, Flask required. No other services (no SQL server) needed.\npip install flask --break-system-packages\n```\n\nNo build step \u2014 this is a flat Python/Flask project. Clone or unzip it\nanywhere; every script self-locates its own root via `SCRIPT_PATH`.\n\n## Usage\n\nStart the admin app (recommended entry point on Android/Termux):\n\n```bash\npython3 pydroid_start.py\n# \u2192 launches src/web/BEJSON_CMS_Admin.py on http://127.0.0.1:5001\n```\n\nOr launch any individual service directly through the modular launcher, which\nensures only one Flask process runs at a time:\n\n```bash\n./cms_launcher.sh admin       # BEJSON_CMS_Admin.py      :5001\n./cms_launcher.sh editor      # BEJSON_CMS_PageEditor.py\n./cms_launcher.sh editorv2    # BEJSON_CMS_PageEditorV2.py\n./cms_launcher.sh publisher   # BEJSON_CMS_Publisher.py\n./cms_launcher.sh profiles    # BEJSON_CMS_ProfileManager.py\n```\n\nManage content headlessly (no Flask server required) with `cms-manage.py` or\nthe standalone CLI shipped in Anthropic's `bejson-cms-manager` skill:\n\n```bash\npython3 src/cms-manage.py status\npython3 bejson_cms_cli.py --project . add-page --title \"New Post\" \\\n    --category BEJSON --html-file body.html\n```\n\nPublish the live database to a static site:\n\n```\nOpen BEJSON_CMS_Publisher.py's web UI (Interface > Publish) and click Build,\nor POST to its /build route. Output lands in storage/builds/.\n```\n\nSet `CMS_PASSWORD` before exposing any service beyond localhost \u2014 it defaults\nto `changeme` and prints a loud startup warning if left unset.\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\nsrc/web/            Six Flask apps (Admin + its 4 Blueprints, PageEditor,\n                     PageEditorV2, ProfileManager, Publisher)\nsrc/lib/             CMSCore + BEJSON/MFDB core libraries, cli/ standalone tools\nstorage/mfdb/         Live database: site_master manifest + entity files,\n                     pages_db/ (per-page content), assets/, standalone_apps/\nstorage/builds/       Generated static site output (regenerated on publish)\nstorage/tmp/          Import staging + service logs (wiped on factory reset)\nresources/            HTML skeleton templates + dark/light stylesheets +\n                     seeded default brand assets\ndocs/                 This documentation set\ntests/                pytest suite (path guard + MFDB validator coverage)\n```\n\n## License\n\nThis project is licensed under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 \u2014 free for\npersonal, educational, research, and non-commercial use. Commercial use\nrequires a separate agreement with the copyright holder. See `LICENSE`.\n",

      "# Security Policy\n\n## Reporting a Vulnerability\n\nReport vulnerabilities to boehnenelton2024@gmail.com. Do not open a public\nissue for unpatched security problems.\n\n## Known operational hardening notes\n\n- All admin routes require authentication via `CMS_PASSWORD`. It defaults to\n  `changeme` \u2014 set a real value via the `CMS_SECRET_KEY`/`CMS_PASSWORD`\n  environment variables before exposing any service beyond `127.0.0.1`. A\n  startup banner and a persistent dashboard alert both fire whenever the\n  default is still in use.\n- Standalone-app ZIP imports are guarded against decompression-bomb style\n  attacks: total uncompressed size is checked from the ZIP's own central\n  directory (`zipfile.ZipInfo.file_size`) before any extraction happens,\n  capped at 300MB.\n- `pydroid_start.py` invokes `termux-open-url` via `subprocess.run()` with an\n  argument list (no shell string interpolation) \u2014 do not reintroduce\n  `os.system()`/shell-string patterns for any subprocess call that could ever\n  carry user-influenced input.\n- Path handling for asset/app serving routes goes through\n  `lib_bejson_Core_bejson_path_guard.py` \u2014 do not bypass it with raw\n  `open()`/`send_file()` calls built from unvalidated request input.\n",

      "# Report: `cms-manage.py` Is Disconnected From \u2014 And Schema-Incompatible With \u2014 the Live CMS\n\n**Date:** 2026-08-08\n**Severity:** High (at time of writing \u2014 see status update below)\n**Status:** \u26a0\ufe0f **SUPERSEDED, pkg81.** This report describes the pkg80\nmid-remediation state (`status`/`category`/`navlink`/`config` converted,\n`author`/`page`/`asset`/`app`/`ad`/`backup`/`restore`/`mount`/`commit`\nstill disconnected). All of those were converted in pkg81, and `cmd_status`'s\nown output text was corrected in pkg113 to stop describing this stale state.\nCurrent status, kept up to date: `docs/security-notes.md`. This file is\nkept only for the entity-by-entity field-shape compatibility table in \u00a72\nbelow, which has lasting reference value; everything else here is history,\nnot current state.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Summary\n\n`src/cms-manage.py`, the project's own CLI toolkit, does not manage the CMS\nyou actually run. It reads and writes a completely separate copy of the\ndatabase, in a different location, and \u2014 this is the part that wasn't known\nwhen this was first flagged at pkg78 \u2014 **using different, incompatible\nschemas** for essentially every entity checked. This is not a \"wrong folder\"\nbug. Every write path in the CLI, if it were pointed at the live database\nwithout further changes, would either fail outright (BEJSON's positional\nfield-count integrity would reject a mismatched row) or \u2014 in the worse case \u2014\nwrite a wrong-shaped row that silently corrupts live data the next time a\nFlask app reads it.\n\n## 2. How the two systems differ\n\nThe live CMS (all 6 Flask apps: Admin's 4 Blueprints, both page editors, the\nPublisher, the Persona Hub) uses `CMSCore` (`lib_bejson_CMS_cms_core.py`)\nagainst one manifest:\n\n```\nstorage/mfdb/site_master/104a.mfdb.bejson\n```\n\n`cms-manage.py` uses a different class, `MFDB_CMS_Manager`\n(`lib_bejson_CMS_cms_mfdb.py`), against a **workspace** populated by\nextracting `.zip` archives:\n\n```\nstorage/workspace/db_global/104a.mfdb.bejson    (from global_master.mfdb.zip)\nstorage/workspace/db_content/104a.mfdb.bejson   (from content_master.mfdb.zip)\n```\n\nNeither archive exists anywhere in this project. `mount_system()` doesn't\nerror when they're missing \u2014 it silently bootstraps a brand-new **empty**\nworkspace instead, which is how this went unnoticed: every command still\n\"works,\" it just works against a private empty universe.\n\nThat much was known at pkg78. What's new this session, from actually reading\n`MFDB_CMS_Manager`'s method bodies rather than assuming its schema matches\nthe live one, is that **the two systems disagree about the shape of almost\nevery entity they both claim to manage:**\n\n| Entity | Live schema (`CMSCore` / real Flask apps) | `MFDB_CMS_Manager`'s schema |\n|---|---|---|\n| Category | `category_name, category_slug` (2 fields) | `name, slug, description, feed_type` (4 fields) \u2014 writes `[name, slug, description, feed_type]` |\n| AuthorProfile | `auth_name, auth_bio, auth_img` (3 fields, **name-keyed**, no UUID) | `author_uuid, name, bio, image_url` (4 fields, **UUID-keyed**) \u2014 `update_author()`/`delete_author()` both look up by `author_uuid`, a field that doesn't exist in the live entity at all |\n| NavLink | `nav_label, nav_url` (2 fields) | `label, url, order` (3 fields) \u2014 writes `[label, url, order]` |\n| SiteConfig | `config_key, config_value` (2 fields) | `config_key, config_value, description` (3 fields) |\n| Page content | One `PageRecord` row (10 fields) + a standalone `pages_db/<uuid>.json` content file, **not** an entity in any manifest | A `Page` entity row **and** a separate `PageContent` entity row, both inside `content_manifest` \u2014 a different manifest than Category/Author/NavLink/SiteConfig, which live in `global_manifest` |\n\nEvery single entity checked diverges \u2014 in field count, field names, key\nstrategy, or all three. The Page/PageContent case is the most serious: it\nisn't a field-shape mismatch, it's a completely different storage\n*mechanism* (two manifest-backed entities vs. one manifest row + one\nstandalone file).\n\n## 3. How this was verified\n\nNot by reading code and assuming \u2014 by running it and, separately, by reading\nevery method body actually invoked by each CLI command before touching\nanything:\n\n- Ran `python3 cms-manage.py mount`, then `category list` \u2014 got back only\n  the bootstrap default `[\"Uncategorized\"]`.\n- Queried the real live site at the same moment via `CMSCore` directly \u2014\n  got back `[\"Uncategorized\", \"BEJSON\"]`, i.e. a real category (and every\n  page under it) that the CLI cannot see at all.\n- Confirmed via `find` that no `.zip` archive exists anywhere under the\n  project root, so `mount_system()`'s \"already have real archives\" branch\n  has never actually run in this project \u2014 every mount to date has taken\n  the empty-bootstrap path.\n- Read `add_category()`, `add_author()`/`update_author()`/`delete_author()`,\n  `add_nav_link()`, `add_global_config()`, and `update_page()`/\n  `delete_page()` directly, line by line, and compared each row shape / key\n  field against the corresponding live `.bejson` manifest file's `Fields`\n  list (not against older documentation, which itself turned out to be\n  stale in places this session).\n\n## 4. Impact\n\n- Every `cms-manage.py` data command silently operates on a disconnected,\n  effectively-empty dataset. None of it reflects, or can modify, the real\n  site.\n- If someone had previously tried to \"fix\" this by simply repointing the\n  manager's paths at the live manifest locations \u2014 the obvious first\n  instinct, and the one this investigation initially assumed would be the\n  fix \u2014 every write command would have produced malformed rows on the first\n  real use: wrong field count against BEJSON's positional-integrity model,\n  wrong field names, and for authors specifically, a lookup key\n  (`author_uuid`) that doesn't exist in the real entity at all.\n- The CLI's `backup`/`restore`/`mount`/`commit` commands are built entirely\n  around the `.zip`-archive model and have no equivalent concept in the live\n  system (which has no archive step at all \u2014 `CMSCore` writes straight to\n  the manifest). These commands need a decision, not a mapping.\n\n## 5. Remediation\n\nThe only safe fix is switching `cms-manage.py` off `MFDB_CMS_Manager` and\nonto `CMSCore` \u2014 the same data-access layer every Flask app already uses \u2014\nentity by entity, translating each command's semantics to match the real\nschema rather than assuming a path swap is enough.\n\n**Started this session** (verified working against live data, detailed\nbelow in the delivered package's changelog):\n- `status`\n- `category` (add / update / delete / list) \u2014 straightforward: live schema\n  is a strict subset of the old one (drops `description`/`feed_type`, which\n  the live `Category` entity has no field for)\n- `navlink` (add / delete / list) \u2014 same pattern, drops the unsupported\n  `order` field\n- `config` (set / list) \u2014 same pattern, drops `description`\n\n**Deliberately not touched yet \u2014 each needs a decision, not just code:**\n- **`author`** \u2014 the old CLI's `update`/`delete` are UUID-keyed; the real\n  entity is name-keyed with no UUID field at all. Options: (a) key CLI\n  author commands by name instead, matching the live entity exactly, or\n  (b) add a `auth_uuid` field to the live `AuthorProfile` schema so both\n  models can agree \u2014 that's a schema migration touching every Flask route\n  that already reads `AuthorProfile`, not a CLI-only change. Recommend (a)\n  unless there's a reason the live schema needs a UUID that hasn't come up\n  yet.\n- **`page`** \u2014 the real content model splits a page across a manifest row\n  (`PageRecord`) and a standalone JSON file (`pages_db/<uuid>.json`, the\n  two-part write contract documented in the `bejson-cms-manager` skill).\n  The old CLI assumed both title and body lived in manifest-backed entities\n  (`Page` + `PageContent`). This is the biggest of the three \u2014 it's not a\n  field rename, it's matching an entirely different write contract.\n- **`asset`** / **`app`** / **`ad`** \u2014 not yet audited to the same depth as\n  the four above; likely have their own field-shape gaps and should be\n  checked with the same method (read the manager's method body, diff\n  against the live manifest's actual `Fields` list) before converting,\n  rather than assumed compatible because they weren't flagged yet.\n- **`backup`** / **`restore`** / **`mount`** / **`commit`** \u2014 archive-model\n  concepts with no live-system equivalent. Needs a product decision: keep a\n  backup/restore concept at all (and if so, define what it means against a\n  manifest with no archive step), or drop these commands.\n\n## 6. What shipped this session\n\n`get_manager()` was replaced with a `get_db()` helper returning a `CMSCore`\ninstance pointed at the real `storage/mfdb/site_master/104a.mfdb.bejson`.\n`cmd_status`, the `category` and `navlink` command groups, and `config\nset`/`config list` were rewritten against `CMSCore`'s actual API\n(`get_records`/`add_record`/`update_record`/`delete_record`) and the real\nfield names. Every rewritten command was tested against the live project\ndata, not just import-checked \u2014 see the delivered package's\n`.bejson_project.json` changelog entry for the exact verification steps.\nThe remaining commands (`author`, `page`, `asset`, `app`, `ad`, `backup`,\n`restore`, `mount`, `commit`) still call `MFDB_CMS_Manager` exactly as\nbefore \u2014 **still disconnected, unchanged, not made worse** \u2014 pending the\ndecisions in \u00a75.\n",

      "# Architecture\n\n## Components\n\n**BEJSON_CMS_Admin.py** \u2014 the registered Flask entry point. Imports and\nregisters four Blueprints with no URL prefix (routes are flat/absolute, e.g.\n`/pages`, not `/content/pages`), plus a global `before_request` auth hook so\nevery admin route requires authentication (a real gap \u2014 roughly 48 of ~50\nroutes had none \u2014 closed in a full sweep).\n\n- **System cube** (`BEJSON_CMS_System.py`) \u2014 dashboard stats, `SiteConfig`\n  key/value editing, factory reset (`/reset`, `/reset/confirm`), the\n  `_ensure_uncategorized_category()` and `_seed_default_brand_and_author()`\n  self-heal routines that run on every startup so a permanent\n  `Uncategorized` category and a default author/brand-asset set survive even\n  a full wipe.\n- **Content cube** (`BEJSON_CMS_Content.py`) \u2014 `PageRecord` CRUD + duplicate,\n  `Category` CRUD, `StandaloneApp` CRUD (ZIP-extract with a 300MB\n  uncompressed-size guard checked from the ZIP's central directory, no\n  decompression needed), `AuthorProfile` CRUD, and the HTML-import pipeline\n  (preview \u2192 confirm \u2192 per-item processing via `/api/import/process_item`).\n- **Media cube** (`BEJSON_CMS_Media.py`) \u2014 `MediaAsset`/`ExternalMedia` CRUD.\n  Uploads stream straight to disk, then a job dict is queued; a single serial\n  background worker (`_asset_worker`) does hashing/dedup/DB-registration/\n  thumbnailing one file at a time, sleeping and calling `gc.collect()`\n  between jobs to bound peak memory on constrained hardware.\n- **Interface cube** (`BEJSON_CMS_Interface.py`) \u2014 the CMS's own home page,\n  `NavLink`/`SocialLink`/`AdUnit` config, and the `/publish` trigger that\n  hands off to `BEJSON_CMS_Publisher.py`.\n\n**BEJSON_CMS_PageEditor.py** (\"V1\") and **BEJSON_CMS_PageEditorV2.py** (\"V2\")\nare separate standalone Flask apps, not Blueprints of the Admin app. Both\nread/write the same page-content contract (name-based field-map lookups, not\nfixed positional indices) and are confirmed cross-compatible \u2014 a page created\nin one loads and saves correctly in the other. V2 is API-driven (JSON\nendpoints under `/api/*`) and under active separate development; V1 is the\nolder server-rendered form-based editor. Both include AI generation features\nthat call `lib_cms_persona_writer.py` to layer an `AI_Profile`'s system\ninstruction on top of required task formatting when an author/persona is\nselected. V2's `/api/tasking/*` routes generate through\n`PersonaWriter.generate_with_fallback()` (pkg142) -- a model-cascade +\ntoken-budget architecture ported from the companion React CMS's\nserver-side Gemini proxy: a 429 (quota)/503 (overloaded) response rotates\nto the next key and, once a model's keys are exhausted, the next model in\na fixed fallback list, rather than failing on the first error. The two\nCMS codebases' generation behavior is intentionally kept in sync this way\nrather than diverging.\n\n**BEJSON_CMS_ProfileManager.py** (\"Persona Hub\") manages `AI_Profile` records\n(25 fields \u2014 internal voice/tone/domain/creativity settings for AI page\ngeneration). It upserts a matching `AuthorProfile` row so the persona name\nis selectable as a byline, but never copies the persona's internal\ndescription into the public `auth_bio` field \u2014 those are deliberately\ndecoupled so AI-flavored internal notes never leak onto the live site.\n\n**BEJSON_CMS_Publisher.py** is the static-site generator. It reads every\nentity through `CMSCore`, dispatches page body rendering to polymorphic\nstrategy renderers (`BEJSON_CMS_Renderers.py` \u2014 supporting `StandardPageRenderer`,\n`VideoPageRenderer`, `DocumentPageRenderer`), renders the `resources/templates/*.html`\nskeletons, generates per-page excerpts (`_generate_excerpt()` \u2014 falls back\nto a 30-word plain-text excerpt when no meta description is set), filters ad\nunits by `ad_zone`, and writes the complete output to `storage/builds/`\n(`index.html`, `style.css`, `category/<slug>/`, `page/<category>/<slug>/`,\n`apps/`, `assets/`).\n\n## Canonical Naming Taxonomy & Schema Architecture\n\nAll live database entities adhere to a single source of truth defined in `src/lib/lib_bejson_CMS_taxonomy.py`:\n- **Canonical Field Prefixes**: Every entity's fields use explicit snake_case tags:\n  - `PageRecord` \u2192 `page_` (`page_uuid`, `page_title`, `page_slug`, `page_cat_name`, `page_type`, `page_author_name`, `page_featured_img`, `page_created_at`, `page_external_url`, `page_cat_uuid`, `page_author_uuid`)\n  - `AuthorProfile` \u2192 `author_` (`author_uuid`, `author_display_name`, `author_bio`, `author_avatar_url`)\n  - `MediaAsset` \u2192 `asset_` (`asset_uuid`, `asset_filename`, `asset_original_name`, `asset_file_hash`, `asset_file_size`, `asset_mime_type`, `asset_uploaded_at`)\n  - `ExternalMedia` \u2192 `extmedia_` (`extmedia_uuid`, `extmedia_name`, `extmedia_type`, `extmedia_url`, `extmedia_created_at`)\n  - `Category` \u2192 `cat_` (`cat_uuid`, `cat_name`, `cat_slug`)\n  - `AdUnit` \u2192 `ad_` (`ad_uuid`, `ad_name`, `ad_banner_url`, `ad_target_url`, `ad_zone`, `ad_active`)\n  - `NavLink` \u2192 `nav_` (`nav_uuid`, `nav_display_label`, `nav_target_url`)\n  - `SiteConfig` \u2192 `sys_` (`sys_uuid`, `sys_key`, `sys_value`)\n  - `SocialLink` \u2192 `social_` (`social_uuid`, `social_platform_name`, `social_target_url`)\n  - `StandaloneApp` \u2192 `app_` (`app_uuid`, `app_name`, `app_slug`, `app_description`, `app_entry_file`, `app_featured_img`)\n- **Synthetic UUID Primary Keys**: Every table contains a synthetic `<prefix>_uuid` RFC 4122 v4 primary key column, resolved by name via Field Map Cache (System Development Policy \u00a76.2) rather than a fixed position \u2014 six entities (`Category`, `AuthorProfile`, `MediaAsset`, `NavLink`, `SiteConfig`, `SocialLink`) plus `AI_Profile` had theirs injected after the fact (pkg135, \"give them all uuids\") rather than present from the schema's original design, so its column position varies by how a given live install got it: first for data migrated directly via `tools/migrate_taxonomy.py`, last for anything backfilled by `BEJSON_CMS_System.py`'s self-heal on boot. Correctness never depends on position either way.\n- **`PageRecord`'s `page_cat_uuid`/`page_author_uuid`** (pkg137): a resolvable identity link to the live `Category`/`AuthorProfile` row, kept in sync on every write \u2014 NOT yet what rendering, permalinks, or related-content matching actually use. Every read path (`BEJSON_CMS_Publisher.py` included) still matches on `page_cat_name`/`page_author_name`, the plain strings. The two `_uuid` fields are additive, immune to the rename/case-collision class of bug that the plain-string fields aren't, but converting the read paths to resolve through them instead is a separate, larger, not-yet-made decision.\n\n## Data Flow\n\n```\nBrowser (admin UI)\n     \u2502  form POST / fetch\n     \u25bc\nBlueprint route (System/Content/Media/Interface)\n     \u2502  db.add_record() / update_record() / delete_record()\n     \u25bc\nCMSCore (lib_bejson_CMS_cms_core.py)\n     \u2502  mfdb_core_add_entity_record() / update_entity_record_bulk()\n     \u25bc\nlib_bejson_Core_mfdb_core.py\n     \u2502  per-manifest RLock \u2192 atomic write (.tmp \u2192 fsync \u2192 os.replace)\n     \u25bc\nstorage/mfdb/site_master/104a.mfdb.bejson (manifest)\nstorage/mfdb/site_master/data/<entity>.bejson (entity file)\n```\n\nPage bodies follow a parallel, separate path: `PageRecord` metadata goes\nthrough the flow above, while the actual `html_body` is read/written\ndirectly as a standalone 104db document at\n`storage/mfdb/pages_db/<page_uuid>.json` \u2014 Flask reads it by UUID at request\ntime, it is never registered as a CMSCore \"entity.\"\n\nPublishing is a one-way read: `BEJSON_CMS_Publisher.py` reads the live MFDB\ntree (never writes back to it) and renders `storage/builds/` from scratch,\ncombined with the shared stylesheets in `resources/styles/`.\n\nMedia upload is asynchronous within a single request/process: the HTTP\nrequest only streams the file to disk and enqueues a job; the actual\nhash/dedup/DB-write/thumbnail work happens on the `_asset_worker` background\nthread, decoupled from the request so a slow decode can't hang the whole\napp (a real, previously-shipped bug \u2014 see the seeded project history in\n`.bejson_project.json`).\n\n## Upstream library sync status (checked against CLI_AI-V16-PKG30, pkg143)\n\nThe Core libraries in `src/lib/` are vendored copies of the same Core\nfamily used by the CLI_AI project.   any pages_db/<uuid>.json content files that reference the old filename.\n    Verified to match the live write contract -- no positional indexing, all\n    reads via Field Map Cache. See docs/remediation_checklist.md Issue 1.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        from PIL import Image\n    except ImportError:\n        print(\"Error: Pillow library not found. old_filename -> new_filename\n\n    for asset in pngs:\n        old_name = asset.get(\"asset_filename\", \"\")\n        new_name = old_name.rsplit(\".\", 1)[0] + \".webp\"\n        old_path = assets_dir / old_name\n        new_path = assets_dir / new_name\n\n        if not old_path.exists():\n            print(f\"  SKIP {old_name}: source file not found on disk\")\n            continue\n        if new_path.exists():\n            print(f\"  SKIP {old_name}: {new_name} already exists\")\n            continue\n        if dry_run:\n            print(f\"  DRY-RUN: would convert {old_name} -> {new_name}\")\n            updated_names[old_name] = new_name\n            continue\n\n        # =============================================================================\n# ROUTES \u2014 AD MANAGER (integrated from BEJSON_Ad_Manager.py)\n# =============================================================================\n\n\ndef _strip_word_html(soup):\n    \"\"\"\n    Remove Microsoft Word HTML artefacts from a BeautifulSoup tree.\n    Targets: o:p tags, MsoXxx classes, mso- inline styles, Word section divs,\n    empty paragraphs left by Word, and Word-generated footer boilerplate.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Remove <o:p> tags (Word XML namespace leftovers)\n    for tag in soup.find_all('o:p'):\n        tag.decompose()\n\n    # Remove any tag whose class list contains a \"Mso\" class\n    for tag in soup.find_all(True):\n        classes = tag.get('class', [])\n        if any('Mso' in c for c in classes):\n            tag.unwrap()  # keep inner text, drop the wrapper\n\n    # Remove inline mso- styles but keep the element\n    for tag in soup.find_all(True, style=True):\n        style = tag.get('style', '')\n        if 'mso-' in style:\n            # Strip only the mso-* declarations, leave other styles\n            cleaned = '; '.join(\n                p for p in style.split(';') if 'mso-' not in p.lower()\n            ).strip().strip(';')\n            if cleaned:\n                tag['style'] = cleaned\n            else:\n                del tag['style']\n\n    # Remove Word section divs\n    for tag in soup.find_all('div', id=re.compile(r'WordSection|Section\\d', re.I)):\n        tag.unwrap()\n    for tag in soup.find_all('div', class_=re.compile(r'WordSection|Section\\d', re.I)):\n        tag.unwrap()\n\n    # Remove footer / boilerplate elements that contain only Word/AI watermark text\n    _WATERMARK_PATTERNS = re.compile(\n        r'(microsoft\\s+word|generated\\s+by|created\\s+with|renderer:|'\n        r'claude\\s+ai|gemini\\s+ai|openai|chatgpt|copilot)',\n        re.I\n    )\n    for tag in soup.find_all(['footer', 'div', 'p', 'span']):\n        Tag_Preview_Text = tag.get_text(strip=True)\n        # Only remove short boilerplate nodes (< 200 chars) matching watermark patterns\n Root cause of the original freezes turned out\n# to be Pydroid3-specific memory/battery-management crashes on the user's\n# device (confirmed resolved by switching to Termux + wakelock) \u2014 not purely\n# a code bug. Rebuilding anyway with deliberately low peak-memory design so\n# it stays safe on constrained devices generally:\n#   - No multiprocessing. Forking duplicates this whole process's memory\n#     footprint at fork time \u2014 the worst possible thing to do when memory is\n#     already tight. A single serial background THREAD is used instead\n#     (shares memory, no copy, still keeps the request thread non-blocking).\n#   - PIL draft() mode: for JPEG, this tells the decoder to decode at a\n#     reduced DCT scale (1/2, 1/4, 1/8) DURING decode, so a large photo is\n#     never fully decoded at full resolution in memory at all.\n#   - Hard pixel-count cap checked from the header (Image.open() only reads\n#     header bytes, no pixel decode) before any decode is attempted.\n#   - Uploads are streamed straight to disk via Werkzeug's f.save(); this\n#     code never calls f.read() on a whole upload.\n#   - Hashing reads in fixed-size chunks; never loads a whole file into RAM.\n# =============================================================================\nTHUMB_SIZE = 320\n_THUMB_MAX_SOURCE_PIXELS = 40_000_000  # ~40MP header-check cap; skip thumbnailing anything larger rather than risk a big decode\n_THUMBABLE_EXT = {'.png', '.jpg', '.jpeg', '.gif', '.webp'}\n\ndef _yt_id_from_url(raw: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Same extraction rule as ytIdFromUrlV2() in BEJSON_CMS_PageEditorV2.py's\n    JS -- kept identical on purpose so a link that embeds correctly there\n    also gets a correct thumbnail here, and vice versa.
